title: introduce-workload-stamped-baseline-artifacts-and-anchored-release-blurbs
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Adds a new artifact type (workload-stamped baseline) to the model intake pipeline, stores per-variant performance fingerprints, and wires a small release-blurb generator that anchors automated changelog lines to concrete workload signatures and delta statistics.
Motivation: We frequently produce generic release notes that lack workload context (e.g. which latency/throughput profile was used). This makes rollouts and canaries noisy. Workload-stamped baselines let us: 1) capture a lightweight, reproducible workload signature alongside numeric baselines; 2) attach those signatures to profiles and releases so release blurbs can say: 'Baseline run: text-generation-short-2k, p95=120ms, delta vs previous +8% tokens/sec'.
Implementation details:
- New artifact type: "baseline.jsonl" entries include: model_alias, variant, workload_tag, seed_hash, sample_counts, perf_metrics (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec), env_hint (quantized/float16), and sample_digest.
- Ingest flow: onboarder writes baseline artifacts as a sidecar when a profiling job completes. The registry now indexes workload_tag -> [variant footprints], and stores sample_digest for quick sampling during regen.
- Release blurb generator: lightweight Python function that picks the most representative baseline for the released variant and formats a terse one-line blurb with strengthening heuristics (prefer matching workload_tag, otherwise nearest neighbor by sample_digest cosine on precomputed embedding).
- Safe defaults: If no baseline exists, blurb falls back to 'no baseline - recommend profile run' and flags the release notes.
- Storage: artifacts stored under /artifacts/baselines/{model_alias}/{variant}/{baseline_id}.jsonl (S3-backed path in metadata)
- Rollout: feature gated behind registry flag 'workload_baselines.enabled' and toggled off by default.
Testing & validation:
- Added unit tests for ingest/serializer and blurb heuristics.
- End-to-end smoke: local simulated profiling job generates a baseline and the release generator produces a blurb.
- Benchmarked indexing cost: indexing adds ~3% to intake latency for large manifests (measured in CI perf job).
Backwards compatibility & migration:
- Existing manifests without baselines are unaffected.
- We add a background migration worker that compacts older profile files into baseline artifacts for the last 30 days (opt-in).
Checklist:
- [x] Schema for baseline artifact and indexer
- [x] Ingest hook in onboarder
- [x] Release blurb generator and small templating engine
- [x] Unit & integration tests
- [x] Documentation PR (docs/registry/baselines.md)
- [x] Feature flag gate and rollout plan
Related: Linear ENG-3141, PM-1985. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3141/workload-stamped-baseline-artifacts-and-release-blurbs

b7c9e21: write ingest hook to append baseline to manifest upload flow
c3d2f9a: implement baseline indexer and s3 path resolver
d4e5a6b: add release_blurb generator and simple templating
e5f6a7c: tests + docs + feature flag wiring
review_comments: Diego Rivera: Can we avoid storing raw sample data in S3 for privacy-sensitive models? Suggest we store only a sample_digest and a small anonymized histogram.
Maya Chen: Good point — updated serializer to redact prompt text and only keep token-length distributions and sample_digest. See commit b7c9e21.
Priya Nair: The nearest-neighbor fallback uses embedding comparisons; how expensive is that at scale? Please add an eviction plan for stale baselines.
Maya Chen: Added an LRU compaction policy to indexer (configurable) and a nightly job to prune baselines older than configured TTL. See indexer changes in c3d2f9a.
Liam O'Connor: Tests look good. One nit: release_blurb.py should include model variant semver if present.
release_notes: Introduce workload-stamped baseline artifacts and an anchored release blurb generator. Adds baseline schema, ingest hook, indexer, and a templated blurb generator that attaches workload context to release notes. Feature gated; safe fallbacks when no baselines are present.
notes_for_ops: Feature is behind flag workload_baselines.enabled=false by default. To enable in Dedicated/Private installs set infra.feature_flags: workload_baselines.enabled=true and ensure S3 bucket path is writable by registry. Migration worker is opt-in and may incur additional S3 read costs.
merge_commit_summary: Squashed commit of the baseline artifact schema, indexer, and blurb generator plus tests and docs. Feature gated behind workload_baselines.enabled.
post_merge_actions: Enable feature flag in staging and run migration worker on a small subset of recent manifests
Add perf job baseline-indexer to nightly CI to monitor indexing cost
Notify solutions and support with a short playbook for interpreting blurb deltas
